tasks.title: Laravel security fix in this repo (project root): harden the staff photo upload — real MIME validation + safe generated filename. Files: app/Http/Requests/HumanResources/Staff/StaffRequestStore.php and StaffRequestUpdate.php (both have the rule 'image' => 'nullable|file|max:5120|mimes:jpeg,jpg,png,bmp' at ~line 50), and app/Http/Controllers/HumanResources/HRDept/StaffController.php (store() ~lines 90-110 and update() ~lines 250-275). The current validation is extension-only (mimes:) so a double-extension file like evil.jpg.php is accepted, and the stored filename is built from the CLIENT-SUPPLIED original name plus the RAW username: $fil = $request->file('image')->getClientOriginalName(); $file = Str::of($fil)->trim(); $ext = $request->file('image')->getClientOriginalExtension(); $currentDate = Carbon::now()->format('Y-m-d-H-i-s'); $fileName = $currentDate.'_'.$request->username.'_'.$file; then storeAs('public/user_profile', $fileName). $request->username can carry path-traversal characters and the original client name is untrusted. Fix: (1) in BOTH form requests, replace the image rule with a MIME-based check: 'image' => 'nullable|file|max:5120|mimetypes:image/jpeg,image/png,image/bmp' (Laravel's mimetypes rule inspects the real file MIME via finfo, closing the double-extension bypass; keep the existing max size 5120). Leave the commented-out 'document' rule line untouched. (2) In StaffController store() and update(), replace the four filename-building lines with a generated, sanitized filename that uses only the timestamp prefix, Str::slug($request->username) and the extension GUESSED FROM THE FILE's real MIME: $currentDate = Carbon::now()->format('Y-m-d-H-i-s'); $fileName = $currentDate.'_'.Str::slug($request->username).'.'.$request->file('image')->guessExtension(); — never embed getClientOriginalName() and never concatenate the raw username; store only this generated filename in the DB (the existing $data += ['image' => $fileName] and storeAs('public/user_profile', $fileName) lines stay). Str is already imported in the controller. Do not change any other behavior in these methods. Then run php -l on every changed file and php artisan test to confirm nothing broke.

Laravel security fix in this repo (project root): upgrade the remaining document-upload validation sites from extension-only mimes: rules to real MIME (mimetypes:) rules. Sites (search for 'mimes:' in each file): app/Http/Controllers/HumanResources/AjaxController.php (uploaddoc method, ~line 1021: 'document' => 'required|file|max:5120|mimes:jpeg,jpg,png,bmp,pdf,doc,docx'), app/Http/Controllers/API/AjaxSupportController.php (~line 2611, same document rule), app/Http/Controllers/HumanResources/HRDept/LeaveController.php (~line 210: 'document' => 'nullable|file|max:5120|mimes:jpeg,jpg,png,bmp,pdf,doc,docs,csv,xls,xlsx'), app/Http/Requests/HumanResources/Leave/HRLeaveRequestStore.php (~line 37: 'document' => 'sometimes|file|max:5120|mimes:jpeg,jpg,png,bmp,pdf,doc,docx'). For EACH live rule, replace mimes:jpeg,jpg,png,bmp,pdf,doc,docx with the equivalent mimetypes: list image/jpeg,image/png,image/bmp,application/pdf,application/msword,application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document (for the LeaveController rule that also allows csv/xls/xlsx, append text/csv,application/vnd.ms-excel,application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet; the 'docs' token there is a typo for docx — map it to the docx MIME, do not invent a separate entry). Keep the exact same required/nullable/sometimes|file|max:5120 prefix and all messages. ALSO inspect the upload handler in AjaxController::uploaddoc (and any other site that stores the file): if the stored filename is built from getClientOriginalName() or the raw request value, switch it to a generated name — timestamp prefix + Str::slug() of a stable identifier (username/staff id where available) + the extension from $request->file('document')->guessExtension() — store only that generated name, never the client name. Do not touch commented-out code. Then run php -l on every changed file and php artisan test to confirm nothing broke.

Write a unit test for the upload hardening in this repo (project root) and run the test suite. Create tests/Unit/UploadValidationTest.php: a plain PHPUnit test (no database) with source-level guards: (1) read app/Http/Requests/HumanResources/Staff/StaffRequestStore.php and StaffRequestUpdate.php as strings and assert the live 'image' rule line contains 'mimetypes:image/jpeg,image/png,image/bmp' and does NOT contain 'mimes:jpeg,jpg,png,bmp' (be comment-aware: strip '//' comment lines before matching so the commented-out document rule cannot false-fail the test); (2) read app/Http/Controllers/HumanResources/HRDept/StaffController.php as a string and assert it contains Str::slug($request->username) and contains guessExtension(), and does NOT contain getClientOriginalName() anywhere and does NOT contain the raw filename-concatenation pattern $request->username.'_'.$file; (3) read app/Http/Controllers/HumanResources/AjaxController.php, app/Http/Controllers/API/AjaxSupportController.php, app/Http/Controllers/HumanResources/HRDept/LeaveController.php and app/Http/Requests/HumanResources/Leave/HRLeaveRequestStore.php as strings and assert each contains 'mimetypes:' and contains 'application/pdf' (comment-aware), and assert the old patterns 'mimes:jpeg,jpg,png,bmp,pdf,doc,docx' and 'mimes:jpeg,jpg,png,bmp,pdf,doc,docs,csv,xls,xlsx' no longer appear in live (non-comment) lines. Run php artisan test — the suite must stay green (currently 35 passing tests / 113 assertions) — and report the run result with the test report contract.
